Phase A missed non-English collateral ligament ruptures ('IKB-Läsion', 'esguince LCM', 'iç yan bağ rüptürü'). Prevalence is 2-3%.
Phase A missed non-English tear terms ('Innenmeniskusriss', 'rotura menisco medial', 'medial menisküs yırtığı', 'латерален скъсване'). True symptomatic prevalence is 5-8%.
Phase A missed non-English lateral tear expressions. True symptomatic prevalence is 2-4%.
Captures advanced joint space loss and tricompartmental osteoarthritis in non-English reports. Prevalence is 0.66%.
Captures advanced lateral compartment osteoarthritis in non-English reports. Prevalence is 0.25%.
Remediated severity gates strictly suppressed mild grade 1/2 chondromalacia without osteoarthritis features (0.0048 -> 0.0032), ensuring only true advanced osteoarthritis is labeled.

Phase A baseline required narrow English keyword 'effusion' and missed German 'Gelenkerguss', Spanish 'derrame articular', Turkish 'eklem içi sıvı', and Dutch 'gewrichtsvocht'. Knee MRI clinical prevalence is typically 10-15% in symptomatic patient cohorts.
Phase A lacked coverage of synovial thickening/proliferation ('Synovialisreizung', 'engrosamiento sinovial', 'sinovyal hipertrofi'). Symptomatic knee cohorts exhibit 8-12% reactive synovitis.
Phase A missed popliteal fossa cyst phrasings ('Bakerzyste', 'quiste de Baker', 'popliteal kist', 'gastrocnemio-semimembranoso bursa'). Symptomatic population prevalence is 7-10%.
Phase A missed non-English bone marrow edema ('Knochenmarködem', 'edema óseo trabecular', 'kemik iliği ödemi', 'botoedeem'). Post-traumatic/symptomatic prevalence is 7-10%.
Phase A baseline missed occult/subchondral fracture terms ('trabekuläre Infraktion', 'fractura subcondral'). True prevalence is 2-3% in acute/subacute MRIs.
